Proxy-SVAR (external instrument) identification

Source: R/psvar.R
varm_proxy.Rd

Mertens & Ravn (2013) / Stock & Watson (2012) proxy identification of one structural shock in a reduced-form varm() fit. The impact vector is \(\gamma = T^{-1}\sum_t u_t m_t\) (covariance of the reduced-form residuals with the proxy), scaled so that the impact response of target equals size. Responses are \(\Theta_h \gamma\), reusing the MA machinery of irf(). Bands come from the proxy wild bootstrap (Rademacher weights applied jointly to the residuals and the proxy, Jentsch & Lunsford 2019).

varm_proxy(
  fit,
  m,
  target = 1L,
  size = 1,
  horizon = 20L,
  nboot = 500L,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9)
)

Arguments

fit

a varm() object.

m

proxy: numeric vector (or one-column matrix) of length nrow(fit$Y), aligned with the data (the first p values are dropped to match the residuals).

target

variable (name or position) whose impact response is normalised to size.

size

size of the shock (impact response of target).

horizon

maximum horizon (impact is 0).

nboot

number of wild-bootstrap draws (0 for point estimates only).

level

confidence levels; bands are equal-tailed percentiles.

Value

a varm_proxy object: estimate ((H+1) x K), draws ((H+1) x K x nboot), bands ((H+1) x K x 2*length(level)), gamma, fstat (see proxy_fstat()).

Details

This does not fit the id_* interface because irf() maps (B, Sigma) to impact matrices, whereas a proxy also needs the residuals and the instrument.

Examples

set.seed(1)
e <- matrix(rnorm(400), 200)
y <- matrix(0, 200, 2)
for (t in 2:200) y[t, ] <- 0.5 * y[t - 1, ] + c(e[t, 1] + 0.3 * e[t, 2], e[t, 2] + 0.5 * e[t, 1])
fit <- varm(y, p = 1)
varm_proxy(fit, m = e[, 1] + rnorm(200, sd = 0.5), horizon = 8, nboot = 100)
#> <varm_proxy> shock to y1 (size 1), horizon 0..8, 100 wild-bootstrap draws
#> first-stage F = 428.8; robust F = 441.7
